principles: Keep decision-doc promotion explicit rather than automatic.
Trust only structured proposal digests and source decision digests for save-time freshness.
Preserve local workflow evidence as separate from Authority receipt completion.
Use existing Lattice scope and process fact surfaces instead of inventing parallel gates.
drivers: The user approved implementing the B-16eb audited execution plan.
The command writes durable project policy docs, so accidental scope expansion is high impact.
The first version must be testable through local CLI and existing DONE quorum behavior.

options.name: A: Narrow CLI promotion workflow
pros: Keeps target path and phase permissions tight
Can be covered by focused smoke tests and process fact contract checks
cons: Requires touching several CLI registration and registry files

options.name: B: Manual docs plus reviewer convention
cons: Does not solve discoverable promotion workflow
Leaves scope and freshness discipline to prose

options.name: C: Automatic decision_set to docs sync
pros: Requires fewer operator steps after decision_set
cons: Pollutes durable docs with temporary decisions
Bypasses explicit promotion intent and increases scope expansion risk

rationale: Choose the narrow CLI promotion workflow because it implements the audited B-16eb contract while preserving explicit operator intent, local scope checks, digest freshness, and non-Authority semantics.

preMortem.scenario: decision_doc_save becomes a back door for writing any decision doc during DEV.
preMortem.trigger: The save handler checks only slug validity and confirm:true, but ignores PLAN file declarations, scope contract, or accepted scope extension state.
preMortem.consequence: Agents can expand durable project policy scope after PLAN and bypass the anti-expansion gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Make target path scope coverage a save-time requirement and cover out-of-scope target rejection in smoke tests.

preMortem.scenario: Preview/review evidence goes stale but save still succeeds.
preMortem.trigger: A proposal or source decision changes after preview or reviewer inspection and the save command does not compare stored digests.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers may approve one policy while a different policy is saved.
preMortem.mitigation: Store proposal and source decision digests, require caller-supplied expectedProposalDigest or saved fresh digest validation, and test stale proposal/source decision rejection.

preMortem.scenario: Local promotion is mistaken for Authority completion.
preMortem.trigger: Policy text, process fact registry, or command output uses Authority or productionDone language loosely.
preMortem.consequence: Future gates or users may treat local docs workflow evidence as receipt-backed production completion.
preMortem.mitigation: Register explicit non-Authority wording in COMMAND_POLICIES/process fact contract and test no Authority fields are emitted.

preMortem.scenario: The implementation becomes too broad for one story.
preMortem.trigger: Custom paths, auto-promotion, INIT reviewer save behavior, or Layer4 fields are added because they appear in nearby docs.
preMortem.consequence: The story grows beyond the audited first-version boundary and risks regressions in unrelated lifecycle gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep checklist scope to canonical path commands, tests, registry, and docs clarification only; use scope extension only if the user explicitly approves a new capability.
